articles.title: 'F--k Lane Kiffin' Chanted by Ole Miss Fans in Viral Video During 'College GameDay' Before LSU Game
articles.summary: Ole Miss fans gave Lane Kiffin a not-so-warm welcome in his return to Oxford for the first time since leaving the program for LSU.
articles.body:
Ole Miss fans gave Lane Kiffin a not-so-warm welcome in his return to Oxford for the first time since leaving the program for LSU.

Chants of "f--k Lane Kiffin" could be heard during taping of ESPN's College GameDay the morning before Saturday's rivalry matchup.

Buzz: Kiffin Wants to 'Embarrass' Ole Miss 😈

No. 7 LSU and No. 8 Ole Miss are set to kick off at 7:30 p.m. ET at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium.

The chants likely won't come as a surprise to Kiffin, who prepared for the matchup by getting LSU students to heckle his players as a warm-up for the reaction they might receive at Ole Miss.

Kiffin departed Ole Miss last fall just before the program's first playoff run after accepting a job offer to join LSU ahead of the 2026 season.

Ole Miss has braced for what could be an emotionally-charged matchup by banning LSU colors in the student section, while Mississippi law enforcement is increasing its presence in Oxford this weekend.

Both Kiffin and Ole Miss coach Pete Golding have said their plan is to keep players' focus on the game.

Kiffin said Monday he has told his players they can focus on playing because "there's just going to be so much attention, hatred, everything on me."

Golding said Friday on ESPN's Pat McAfee Show his message was for his team to focus on the way they played in season-opening wins over Louisville and Charlotte.

"Regardless of whether Coach Kiff's on the other side or not, if we're not going to executive our plan at a high level, then we're not going to win," Golding said.

A major factor in Kiffin's hope of winning his first game against his former program is the health of LSU quarterback Sam Leavitt, who On3's Pete Nakos reports has been dealing with throwing shoulder soreness.

Leavitt was listed as doubtful earlier this week before he was removed from the injury report a day before Saturday's kickoff.

articles.title: Atletico Madrid vs Real Madrid: La Liga – preview, team news, prediction
articles.summary: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho admits his team does not know how to control matches before Sunday’s La Liga clash.
articles.body:
Who: Atletico Madrid vs Real Madrid What: La Liga Where: Metropolitano Stadium, Madrid, Spain When: Sunday, September 20, at 4:15pm (14:15 GMT) How to follow: Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up from 11:15 GMT before our live text commentary stream

Atletico host bitter city rivals Real for the Madrid derby as both sides look to keep up with early La Liga pacesetters Barcelona.

Madrid trail unbeaten champions Barcelona at the top of the table by three points, with Atletico third.

Atletico have bounced back from back-to-back defeats to Bilbao and Liverpool earlier in September, beating Real Sociedad 3-0 and Osasuna 4-0 in their last two games.

Real come into the game in decent form under boss Jose Mourinho but have had wobbles this month, with a defeat to Betis and scoring late to beat bottom club Elche after squandering a two-goal lead.

Improving Atletico cruise to win over Osasuna

Atletico Madrid thrashed Osasuna 4-0 on Wednesday to build some form in the run-up to Sunday’s derby clash against rivals Real Madrid.

Jonathan David, Lee Kang-in, Robin Le Normand and Alex Baena’s goals helped Diego Simeone’s side cruise to a comfortable home victory.

They were without injured striker Julian Alvarez, but it did not matter after they secured a second straight win to cut the gap on top two Barcelona and Real Madrid.

The comfortable victory was important for an Atletico side with lots of new faces still bedding in, after two defeats in their three matches prior.

“We controlled it in the first half even though we weren’t clinical,” said coach Diego Simeone. “We were clinical in the second half and controlled the game.”

Real ‌Madrid squandered a two-goal lead before substitute Carlos Espi struck in stoppage time to ⁠secure a dramatic 3-2 ⁠victory at Elche in La Liga on Tuesday.

Real went 2-0 up inside 33 minutes through a Matias Dituro own goal and Kylian Mbappe, but second-half strikes from Abiel ⁠Osorio and Fer Nino hauled Elche level before Espi restored the visitors’ lead in the 91st minute.

It was the second time in ⁠six league matches that the 21-year-old Espi had come off the bench to score a late winner, although Mourinho remained concerned by Real’s failure to control the second half in advance of Sunday’s derby against Atletico Madrid.

“The problem seems obvious to me. It’s harder to know why, but it’s easy to understand that there are matches that seem over and, in the end, aren’t,” said Mourinho.

“[There are] matches where we have three, four, five chances to finish them and don’t,” he said at the pre-match news conference.

“After failing to do so, it feels like we go from ease, because it seemed easy, to losing control.”

Mourinho said his team’s defensive issues were of concern.

“Not just for Sunday’s match, but for every match. I like my team to score goals … but I also like controlling matches,” explained Mourinho.

“I don’t like gifting control. It’s not about the goals, it’s about giving away control of the match.”

The Opta supercomputer has made Real Madrid the favourites, with a win probability of 46.6 percent. Atletico were given a 28.3 percent chance of winning, while a draw was estimated at a 25.1 percent likelihood.

The rivals have faced each other on 243 occasions; Real Madrid won 125 games, Atletico won 60, while 58 matches ended as draws.

March 22, 2026: Real Madrid 3-2 Atletico (La Liga)

January 8, 2026: Atletico 1-2 Real Madrid (Spanish Super Cup semifinal)

September 27, 2025: Atletico 5-2 Real Madrid (La Liga)

March 12, 2025: Atletico 1-0 Real Madrid (Champions League last 16, second leg)

March 4, 2025: Real Madrid 2-1 Atletico (Champions League last 16, first leg)

What happened the last time the two clubs played each other?

Vinicius Jr scored ⁠twice ⁠as Real Madrid fought back to beat Atletico Madrid 3-2 at the Santiago Bernabeu in ⁠a breathless Spanish capital derby in March.

Atletico’s Ademola Lookman opened the scoring in the 33rd minute, finishing a slick ‌counterattack involving Matteo Ruggeri and a delightful back-heel from Giuliano Simeone.

Vinicius equalised from the penalty spot in the 52nd minute, after David Hancko clumsily tripped Brahim Diaz, and Federico ⁠Valverde capitalised on a ⁠Jose Maria Gimenez error three minutes later to make it 2-1 to Real.

Nahuel Molina silenced Real’s ⁠Bernabeu stadium with a thunderous 30-metre strike in ⁠the 66th minute, but ⁠Vinicius restored Real’s lead with a cracking solo effort six minutes later.

What happened in the corresponding fixture last season?

Julian Alvarez scored twice as Atletico Madrid came from behind to thrash city rivals Real Madrid 5-2 in a pulsating derby in September 2025.

Atletico’s aggressive start paid off when Robin Le Normand opened the scoring with a header in the 14th minute.

However, Kylian Mbappe burst through to level with an unstoppable strike from close range in a quick counter in the 25th minute, with Arda Guler netting a volley from a Vinicius Jr cross 11 minutes later to put the visitors in front.

Alexander Sorloth’s header in added time before the break gave Atletico a boost, and they regained the lead five minutes into the second half when Alvarez converted a penalty after Guler’s high boot clipped Nico Gonzalez on the face inside the box.

After Alvarez extended their lead in the 64th minute with a sublime free kick into the top corner, substitute Antoine Griezmann sealed the win in a quick counter in added time.

Alvarez, Pablo Barrios, and Sorloth are doubts, as all three are struggling with muscle issues.

Jonathan David is likely to continue up front if Alvarez is absent or starts on the bench.

Eder Militao, Rodrygo, and Ferland Mendy are unavailable due to injuries, but otherwise Mourinho appears to have a full squad to choose from.

articles.title: Tottenham 2-3 Aston Villa: Winless Spurs drop into relegation zone while visitors secure first win of Premier League season
articles.summary: Report as Spurs suffer another defeat, making it their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign; Spurs only have two points and goal difference of -6, eclipsing their 2008-09 start (2 points, -3 goal difference)
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi's expensively assembled side were hit by goals from Johan Manzambi, Nicolas Jackson and Emi Buendia which handed Villa an important win - their first of the season.

Both clubs had made slow starts to the new campaign after summer rebuilds and while Spurs had failed to score in four league fixtures.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Aston Villa

Conor Gallagher at least got Spurs' first goal of the season late on, followed up by a Jan Paul van Hecke header, but it was nothing more than a consolation and too little too late.

After a bright start from Spurs where they forced Zion Suzuki into four saves inside the first 20 minutes, Villa hit Tottenham with a sucker punch - with captain Micky Van de Ven off the pitch after he took a whack to the face from Tyrone Mings, Manzambi fired in.

Spurs' goal drought appeared over on the hour mark when Sandro Tonali played in Andy Robertson and Mohammed Kudus poked in his cross, but VAR ruled it was offside.

Jackson then made it 2-0 by finding the bottom corner.

A wonderful effort by Buendia from 25 yards made the victory safe for Villa and sparked 'you're getting sacked in the morning' chants by the away faithful.

Ahead of the extended break, Spurs find themselves in the relegation zone and have only won five of their last 36 matches at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

"The pressure heats up," said former Tottenham defender Michael Dawson on Soccer Saturday .

"That's what happens when you finish 17th twice, you spend all this money, there's a huge expectation around the football club. I believed there was going to be a shift but when there isn't, it breeds and now, unfortunately, for Spurs, they've got three weeks to wait until the next game."

The key moments from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium...

9: DOUBLE SAVE! Savio has two bites of the cherry from inside the box but Suzuki reacts to both effort to keep Spurs at bay.

19: INJURY! Pedro Porro limps off, clearly frustrated having pulled what looked like a groin muscle. His replacement Archie Gray is then denied from the angle by Suzuki.

45: OUCH! Van de Ven suffers a nasty blow to his face after clearing a set piece and needs to leave the field to receive treatment.

45+3: GOAL! Villa take advantage of the extra-man by attacking down the left which results in Manzambi scoring his first goal for the club.

58: GOAL RULED OUT! Spurs think they've opened their account for the season through Kudus but Robertson was offside in the build-up, so VAR steps in to disallow the goal.

67: GOAL! Jackson doubles Villa lead, powering a shot into the corner after beating Van de Ven in a duel.

79: GOAL! Buendia puts the result beyond doubt with a stunning finish from 25 yards as Spurs fans head for the exit.

86: SPURS FINALLY SCORE! Sarcastic cheers inside the stadium as Gallagher pokes home from close range to end the Spurs drought.

90+6: GOAL! Van Hecke heads home for 3-2 but the referee blows for full-time just after the restart.

De Zerbi admits he 'didn't speak to players' after defeat

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi on the timing of the international break:

"Maybe it's better, I didn't speak with the players today because I didn't want to say anything.

"But the players who go with the national team they have to play, they have to work and the other players like Gallagher, Solanke, Tosin, Senesi, Savio for sure we have to work more because of the physical condition I didn't like in this game."

He added: "I'm very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated for the performance because we can't lose this game in this way, absolutely. We can't concede the second goal, we can't lose balance just because in the first half we are losing in the beginning of the second half.

"I spoke with the four attackers to use their heads calmly, play calm, play, enjoy, don't take risks. When we conceded the second goal it was incredible."

Villa boss Unai Emery speaking about the performances of Zion Suzuki and Nicolas Jackson:

"They are here for it. Their commitment to us, challenging themselves to achieve what we did before and replacing important players, is fantastic. But every player needs to understand how we can feel better collectively and how they can help us with their qualities, exploiting our best performance.

"Today, we made a clear step forward in improving that. Zion is maintaining the performance he showed before, and Jackson clearly improved from the previous matches. This is the way and the example of how he played."

articles.title: Sergio Camello: "La temporada pasada me propuse disfrutar y ser libre"
articles.standfirst: El atacante madrileño realizó una valoración del encuentro ante Osasuna
articles.summary: El atacante madrileño realizó una valoración del encuentro ante Osasuna
articles.body: Sergio Camello se va contento al parón de selecciones. El delantero anotó su séptimo gol de la temporada y superó su mejor marca en Primera división, además de igualar a Guilherme con 24 goles como máximo goleador rayista en la máxima competición nacional. Después del encuentro, habló sobre su espectacular momento de forma y sobre esa vuelta a Vallecas tan ansiada. Punto en El Sadar: "Puntuar aquí siempre es importante. Hace 20 años que el Rayo no gana aquí y puntuar es bueno para nosotros". Indicaciones de Beñat al descanso: "Nos ha dicho que no tenemos que entrar en su juego de 'gresca', ser nosotros, jugar entre líneas y salir por banda. Así ha llegado el gol". Mejor marca: "Es mi mejor temporada en Primera. Tengo una ambición tremenda. Va a ser un año muy bonito. La temporada pasada me propuse disfrutar y ser libre". Vuelta a Vallecas, tras el parón: "Supone todo volver. No queda ni en anécdota lo de Butarque. Hemos sabido puntuar, pero no es nuestra casa y por fin nos vamos a volver a juntar con nuestra gente que lo ha pasado mal. Nos volveremos a juntar y será una fiesta".

articles.title: Hartlepool United: Lee Clark resigns as head coach after Worthing loss
articles.summary: Lee Clark resigns as Hartlepool United head coach after a sixth loss in seven games following the 3-1 home defeat by Worthing.
articles.body:
Lee Clark resigned as Hartlepool United head coach with immediate effect following their home defeat by Worthing.

The 3-1 loss was a third defeat in a row and a sixth in seven matches, pushing Pools down to 18th before the afternoon kick-offs in the National League.

Clark took over at Victoria Park in the summer after a short spell with Rotherham United at the end of last season, but fans called for his head during Saturday's game as Hartlepool's slump continued.

"I resign from my position with immediate effect," Clark, a former Newcastle, Sunderland and Fulham player, told BBC Radio Tees.

"I wanted to give this club and the fans something to be proud of, what they deserve, but I haven't been able to do that unfortunately."

The former Huddersfield Town and Birmingham City boss added: "I was excited to take the job and I wanted to be the man to get them back to where they need to be and deserve to be, but it hasn't worked out."

Pools were taken over in January by American businessman Landon Smith as the County Durham club aim to end their four-year stay in the National League.

But the search now begins for their ninth permanent manager or head coach in this period outside the English Football League.

articles.title: Lane Kiffin greeted by Ole Miss fans with boos, expletive-laden chants during 'College GameDay' appearance
articles.summary: Ole Miss fans have been waiting for Saturday for many months.
articles.body:
Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford, Mississippi, as head coach of LSU has been one of the most-anticipated matchups of the 2026 college football season . Kiffin will surely get a rude welcome when he steps inside Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on Saturday night.

Hours before LSU and Ole Miss kick off, the vitriol toward Kiffin began with "College Gameday" in town and fans eager to express their displeasure with their former coach.

It didn't take long for the "F*** Lane Kiffin" chants to begin.

The Ole Miss faithful later had the opportunity to make sure Kiffin heard that sentiment directly after he was introduced for an interview during the show.

The anger continued during the interview with fans chanting, " A**hole! A**hole! " before bringing back the "F*** Lane Kiffin" chants as Kiffin spoke to the "Gameday" panel.

Kiffin didn't bite and kept his focus on the game and not everything else surrounding the matchup between the two top-10 teams , which obviously is centered around his departure to LSU .

"You know, both teams have great players, great coaches, have a lot of respect for their program," Kiffin said. "So, we just felt the players performing really well tonight in a really awesome matchup. Two top-10 teams, national game of the week. So, both programs should be really exciting."

Kiffin talked about the emotions swirling around the game and the importance of his players to worry about what matters on the field.

"Obviously, it's going to be there," Kiffin said. "There's going to be some expression for some of these coaches coming back for most points and players coming back, but to play on execution.

"And this will be a really competitive game for a long period of time with a lot of plays. So, you've got to really stay focused and not listen to all the noise and all chatter if you can."

Kickoff for LSU at Ole Miss is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET on Saturday night and will be televised on ABC.

articles.title: Tommy Castellanos-Hammond QB1 Addressed by Texas Tech HC After Replay Ruling Seals Win vs. Houston
articles.summary: After holding on for a 28-26 win over Houston on Friday night, Texas Tech head coach Joey McGuire made it clear Will Hammond is the No. 1 quarterback going forward even though Tommy Castellanos got the start.
articles.body:
After holding on for a 28-26 win over Houston on Friday night, Texas Tech head coach Joey McGuire made it clear Will Hammond is the No. 1 quarterback going forward even though Tommy Castellanos got the start.

Speaking to reporters following the dramatic win, McGuire made it clear Hammond is the Red Raiders' starter and there will be specific packages used for Castellanos:

"Will Hammond is our starting quarterback. We have packages for Tommy, and those packages will continue to grow. We had two plays we're going to run right there. If we don't get pressure, then I think we have a huge play starting right off the bat. ... The plan was two plays and Will come into the game."

Texas Tech held on to win after replay review confirmed Houston quarterback Conner Weigman was tackled down just short of the goal line on a two-point attempt that would have tied the game with 49 seconds remaining.

articles.title: Brighton beat Arsenal 3-0 as Man City top Premier League without playing
articles.summary: Arsenal suffer shock 3-0 loss at Brighton to lose top spot in the Premier League on goal difference to Manchester City.
articles.body:
Arsenal slumped to a first loss in their Premier League title defence – and it was a heavy one at Brighton.

After four straight wins for the champions, the 3-0 defeat at the Amex Stadium on Saturday came out of nowhere. Conceding the third goal from a corner — typically an area of strength for Arsenal – summed up an unusually sloppy performance from Mikel Arteta’s team.

Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas scored in the first half with shots from outside the penalty area, before Chema Andres completed the win with a header at the back post from Gross’s corner.

The victory will have been especially sweet for Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler, who said “only one team tried to play football” after his team’s narrow home loss to Arsenal last season.

Arsenal have often struggled against Brighton, which was the last team to inflict such a heavy defeat on the Gunners in any competition — winning 3-0 at Emirates Stadium in May 2023.

It completed a brilliant week for Brighton, after beating Coventry 5-0 in the league last weekend and coming from two goals down in midweek to beat Manchester United 3-2 away in the English League Cup.

Manchester City — the other team to win their first four games — can now move three points clear in the standings by beating Sunderland on Sunday.

articles.title: Everton 1-0 Ipswich: Thierno Barry extends Toffees unbeaten start despite VAR interference to deny second goal
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights as Thierno Barry scored the winner but was controversially denied a second by VAR; Abdul Fatawu was sent off for two bookable offences; David Moyes' side move up to fifth in the table after extending unbeaten start
articles.body:
James Tarkowski's strike from range hit the striker and wrong-footed Christian Walton to hand David Moyes' side their second victory of the season, extending their unbeaten start and lifting them to fifth in the table.

But Everton arguably should have won by a larger margin. Barry met Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's in-swinging corner with a fine glancing header in the second half, only for VAR to intervene and chalk it off, deeming Brennan Johnson to have been interfering with play from an offside position.

Latest news and rumours: Everton | Ipswich

The incident comes a week on from the heavily scrutinised officiating display in the Manchester derby , where VAR's inaction drew major criticism, forcing Pro Ref to issue a statement of apology. On this occasion, however, VAR's intervention may well cause controversy for the opposite reason.

Speaking on Soccer Saturday , Sue Smith said: "The goal has been ruled out with Johnson deemed to be affecting the goalkeeper, but this is a bad decision. There was no way he was going to save that."

The hosts tried and failed to score many more times. Johnson skewed wide in the first five minutes, while Dewsbury-Hall bookended a poor performance in front of goal by heading inexplicably off target from a perfect Tyler Dibling cross late on. From 21 shots, Everton landed two on target.

In the end, their wastefulness did not matter, with Ipswich unable to make any of their chances stick either. Abdul Fatawu was dismissed for two bookable offences, the second for simulation, before the afternoon was out, with Gary O'Neil left visibly frustrated with his side's lack of quality in the final third. Ipswich registered double Everton's efforts on target but failed to properly test Jordan Pickford.

5: MISS! Johnson flashes wide after being put through smartly by Harrison Armstrong.

9: SAVE! Pickford denies Emersonn at his near post after a needless giveaway from Dewsbury-Hall.

11: GOAL! Tarkowski's strike from distance rebounds fortunately off Barry and wrong-foots Walton to give Everton an early lead.

33: CHANCE! Ainsley Maitland-Niles picks out Barry with a guided cross but the striker has to stoop to meet the delivery and steers off target.

38: MISS! Leif Davis meets Fatawu's lofted cross and is completely unmarked at the back post but manages to casually poke wide.

58: VAR! The video officials send the referee to the pitchside monitor to overturn Barry's second goal after Johnson is deemed to interfere with the goalkeeper's line of sight, despite being nowhere near the ball.

67: RED! Fatawu dismissed for diving having already collected a yellow card for halting an Everton break.

76: MISS! Dewsbury-Hall heads Dibling's teasing cross wide, completely unmarked.

Moyes questions consistency of decision making from VAR

"On the VAR decision, does it affect his [the goalkeeper's] ability to see? I didn't think that was the case. It's difficult for the referees, I understand that.

"Do I think we will get consistency on the same thing throughout the season? I'll be doubtful of that. The goalkeeper wouldn't have saved the header.

"No doubt Brennan is offside, but did he interfere, really? He was never going to save it. Ultimately it didn't make any difference to the result so I'm thankful for that."

On the performance: "We had big chances to go further in front, we didn't. We should have scored more once the player got sent off, Ipswich made it a bit nervy at the end. But we got the job done after a difficult week.

"We're doing a lot of good things but I would have liked it to be better today. Twenty-one shots and two on target, that's not any good."

O'Neil: Only criticism is with lack of finish

"Disappointed with the result, very unfortunate to leave with nothing. The goal is unfortunate.

"The main criticism is we didn't manage to score because we arrived in good areas.

"The final pass, we leave it short. We don't quite make the right decision or execute well enough.

"We felt like we had control. Away from home in the Premier League, the players deserve credit for that. We were competitive."

On the red card : "I've seen them given, seen them not given. He's anticipating contact and, in truth, moves his leg towards it. I've spoken to Abdul, he's a young kid giving us everything, he's got to be a bit more wise when he's on a yellow. He understands that. Our response with 10 men was incredible."

Iowa is back in action as it hosts in-state rival Northern Iowa at 3 p.m. CST. The Hawkeyes find themselves as near-40-point favorites against the FCS Panthers. While Iowa should be the favorite in this game, UNI is going to make sure they earn it.

The Panthers' roster is filled with native Iowans. This game will mean a ton to them as they look to shock the college football world. Kirk Ferentz will need to make sure his team is focused on handling their business in front of them before shifting attention to Big Ten play next week. A win today would give Iowa a perfect 3-0 start to the season and start some interesting conversations about postseason hopes.

articles.title: Queens Park Rangers 2-2 Preston: Paul Smyth strikes equaliser in comeback for 10-man QPR
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Queens Park Rangers and Preston North End at the MATRADE Loftus Road Stadium on Saturday; Paul Smyth scores late equaliser to earn point for 10-man QPR.
articles.body:
Johnny Kenny's first goals for North End - including an opener after 64 seconds - left them in a great position in their first match since the sacking of boss Paul Heckingbottom.

But Kwame Poku pulled a goal back for Rangers midway through the second half and Smyth's late strike rescued a point for the west London side.

A run of six defeats from seven games left Preston bottom of the Sky Bet Championship, and this week cost Heckingbottom his job.

But Irish striker Kenny, a recent signing from Celtic, put them in control at Loftus Road, scoring from the first attack of the game and then doubling their lead after Rangers' Dennis Cirkin had been sent off.

First-team coach Jason Euell, placed in caretaker charge following Heckingbottom's exit, could not have wished for a better start.

Stan Mills' long ball should have been routinely dealt with by Jimmy Dunne near the halfway line, but the R's skipper hesitated and Kenny robbed him before racing through and slotting past goalkeeper Pierce Charles.

Worse followed for Rangers on the quarter-hour mark when Cirkin was shown a red card after clattering into Leo Leroy.

Andrew Hughes should then have made it 2-0 but headed Alfie Devine's cross wide of the target when unmarked.

That was a let-off for Rangers, but they were punished for more sloppy defending in the 26th minute.

Mills burst into the box from the right-hand side, Ronnie Edwards and Nicolas Madsen attempted to stop him but got in each other's way and Kenny met the resulting loose ball with a low first-time shot into the far corner of the net.

That left QPR battling against the odds, but they did create openings, the first of which came just before half-time when Poku was just unable to connect with Kealey Adamson's cross.

Rangers continued to attack after the break and Edwards volleyed wide, substitute Koki Saito also fired past a post, and both Madsen and Amadou Mbengue sent shots over the crossbar.

They were rewarded for their persistence with a goal after 66 minutes - winger Poku's first for the club.

Dunne was crowded out as he tried to flick on Smyth's long throw but Poku skillfully created some space for himself near the edge of the penalty area and thumped a low shot past Daniel Iversen.

Preston then had to cling on, with both teams hitting the woodwork as Rangers searched for an equaliser.

Callum Lang's header from Andrija Vukcevic's cross hit the top of the bar and, at the other end, Alfie Lloyd hit the bar shortly before being denied by Iversen at point-blank range.

Iversen could do nothing about Smyth's 20-yard rocket but did produce another fine save in the final seconds, this time to deny Madsen.

articles.title: Lincoln 1-2 Swansea: Vitor Matos' Swans go top after comeback win
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Sky Bet Championship match between Lincoln City and Swansea City at the ProAmpac Stadium on Saturday; Moussa Yeo and Stephen Eustaquio score quickfire double as Swans hit back for victory.
articles.body:
After an insipid first-half display, the Swans were able to turn the game on its head after the break and, barring a big win for West Brom over Wolves on Sunday, will head into the extended international break top of the pile.

They lead the division by two points, ahead of Middlesbrough, after ending the Imps' five-match unbeaten run, despite them leading at half-time through Reeco Hackett's penalty.

Swansea goalkeeper Lawrence Vigouroux was worked in only the second minute when he got down to save Hackett's low shot after his defence had struggled to clear a corner.

His opposite number, George Wickens, was almost caught unaware when Swansea midfielder Elijah Just attempted to lob him from 45 yards, but he got back to prevent the ball sailing over him.

Hackett then had another opportunity for the Imps when he battled his way into a shooting position, but his strike went into the side-netting.

Vigouroux was fortunate he did not present the home side with the lead in the 22nd minute when he pushed the ball straight to Hackett just outside the area, with the Chile international very relieved to catch the attacker's underhit lob.

Lincoln were then awarded a penalty in the 39th minute when Josh Tymon bundled into the back of Freddie Draper, and Hackett got the goal his first-half performance merited by confidently dispatching from 12 yards.

It was a lead the hosts deserved as they went into half-time, but having been subdued in the first 45 minutes, Swansea came out for the second half firing.

They were level within two minutes of the restart when Melker Widell worked his way to the byline down the right before pulling the ball back for Moussa Yeo to convert from close range.

The turnaround was rapidly completed in the 51st minute when Canada midfielder Eustaquio received the ball from Just before his shot from outside box took a big deflection beyond the helpless Wickens.

Having looked in control before the break, the Imps seemed to lack ideas as they looked to prevent a first league defeat in nearly a month.

The Swans, meanwhile, almost made the game safe when Widell bent an effort narrowly wide from just outside the area.

Widell then almost had a second assist of the afternoon when he moved the ball to the right for Ronald whose shot was beaten away by Wickens as the visitors' second-half resurgence earned all three points.

"We're delighted with the level of performance, especially first half.

"They've gone top of the league today, Swansea, so that's the level of opponent and we made it incredibly uncomfortable for them in the first half.

"We completely dominated the half, loads of volume around their goal and quality from our lads.

"We deserved to score at least one, maybe more, but we got a little warning just before half-time of what they're capable of around our goal, and unfortunately we've had five or six minutes where it was just a little bit too much and they were too sharp for us.

"The second goal is unfortunate - it takes a big deflection and we can't do much about it - but the first goal we'll review and reflect it.

"We'll be annoyed we've not dealt with it better, but the boys in this early part of the season have been incredible."

"It's a nice feeling, of course, but we need to stay grounded as we know there are a lot of games and there is a lot still to compete for.

"We have an international break now, so we will not feel the effect of this game on the next game because it is so far away.

"It is important now to rest the players who will stay with us, keep improving them, keep feeding them in terms of the quality of the [training] sessions, then we're probably going to have the players [back from international duty] the day before Norwich.

"This is a really hard place to come. We knew we had to be really spot-on, in terms of organisation.

"Towards the end of the first half, we were starting to impose much more of ourselves and much more of the game we needed to play.

"Half-time was important for us to refresh and to think how we get momentum back."

What the result means and next fixtures...
